lesson.title: Network Hardware: NICs, MAC Addresses, IP and Routers

images.alt: A device accessing a remote server through a network interface and router.
Examples of correctly formatted MAC, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

questions.prompt: What hardware allows a computer to connect to a network?
Which address format is an IPv4 address?

questions.accepted_answers:
network interface card
network interface controller

questions.prompt: How many bits are in an IPv6 address?
Explain two differences between a MAC address and an IP address.
questions.model_answer: A MAC address identifies a network interface and is usually assigned at manufacture; an IP address is allocated for network communication. MAC addresses are commonly written in hexadecimal pairs; IPv4 is normally dotted decimal or IPv6 hexadecimal groups.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: A MAC address identifies a network interface and is usually assigned at manufacture; an IP address is allocated for network communication.
1: MAC addresses are commonly written in hexadecimal pairs; IPv4 is normally dotted decimal or IPv6 hexadecimal groups.
questions.student_guidance:
Compare what each address identifies and how it is obtained.
Compare how the two kinds of address are normally written.

questions.prompt: Explain two roles of a router on a school network.
questions.model_answer: It forwards packets to destinations between networks. It can connect the local network to the internet or allocate local IP addresses.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: It forwards packets to destinations between networks.
1: It can connect the local network to the internet or allocate local IP addresses.
questions.student_guidance:
Consider what happens to packets travelling between separate networks.
Think about another service a school router might provide locally.
